questions.question: What is true about double or triple trailers?

options.text: They can usually be driven faster than straight trucks.
They are usually less stable than smaller commercial vehicles.
They are always easier to drive than other commercial vehicles.
They do not need a special endorsement to drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are usually less stable than smaller commercial vehicles.
questions.explanation: Double and triple trailers are less stable than single commercial vehicles. They roll over more easily. Drive them slowly and smoothly to prevent rollovers.

questions.question: What can federal inspectors do if your vehicle is unsafe?

options.text: Take you to a garage to fix your vehicle.
Ask you to have your vehicle's problems fixed.
Call a mechanic for you.
Remove your vehicle from service until it is fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove your vehicle from service until it is fixed.
questions.explanation: Federal and state inspectors can put an unsafe vehicle out of service. You cannot drive it until it is fixed.

questions.question: What should you use when parked on the side of the road?

options.text: Only the rear flashing lights.
One set of turn signals.
Your high beam headlights.
Your four-way flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your four-way flashers.
questions.explanation: Always turn on your four-way emergency flashers when parked on the side of the road. This is even more important at night.

questions.question: How can you slow down if your hydraulic brakes fail?

options.text: Shift into a higher gear.
Shift into a lower gear.
Find a hill.
Let the truck run out of gas.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into a lower gear.
questions.explanation: If your hydraulic brakes fail, shift into a lower gear to help slow your vehicle.

questions.question: What is off-tracking?

options.text: The front wheels follow a different path than the rear wheels.
All wheels follow the exact same path.
The load shifts during a turn.
The wheels run over a curb during a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front wheels follow a different path than the rear wheels.
questions.explanation: Off-tracking happens when a vehicle turns a corner. The rear wheels follow a different path than the front wheels.

questions.question: What is true about a tired driver?

options.text: They are extra alert.
They should take over-the-counter pills to stay awake.
They may make important decisions too slowly.
They are usually more careful than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may make important decisions too slowly.
questions.explanation: Tired drivers do not see or react to hazards as quickly as well-rested drivers. They are slow to make important decisions.

questions.question: Most heavy-duty vehicles use ____ air brake systems.

options.text: Single
Dual
Triple
Quad

questions.correctAnswerText: Dual
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles have dual air brake systems.

questions.question: What does the emergency brake system use?

options.text: Only parts of the parking brake system.
Only parts of the service brake system.
Parts of both the parking and service brake systems.
Only parts that are unique to the emergency brake system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Parts of both the parking and service brake systems.
questions.explanation: Air brake systems have three parts: service brakes, parking brakes, and emergency brakes. The emergency brake system uses parts from both the parking and service brake systems.

questions.question: What should you check when looking at a coupling device?

options.text: Look for mud on the fifth wheel.
Make sure the kingpin is polished.
Make sure there is a space between the upper and lower fifth wheel.
Make sure the locking jaws are closed around the kingpin.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure the locking jaws are closed around the kingpin.
questions.explanation: When checking coupling devices, make sure there is no space between the upper and lower fifth wheel. The locking jaws must be securely closed around the kingpin.

questions.question: What is true about trailers built before 1975?

options.text: They must have spring brakes.
They do not need to have spring brakes.
They are unsafe to drive.
They are not allowed on public roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: They do not need to have spring brakes.
questions.explanation: Trailers built before 1975 do not need spring brakes. When parking a trailer without spring brakes, use wheel chocks to keep it from rolling.

questions.question: What does poor weight balance do?

options.text: Improves how a vehicle handles.
Makes it harder to handle a vehicle.
Makes steering easier.
Makes a vehicle easier to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes it harder to handle a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Poor weight balance makes a vehicle unsafe and difficult to handle.

questions.question: Before a trip, how do you check that air reaches all trailers?

options.text: Close the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
Disconnect air supply lines and listen for air escaping.
Detach and reattach the rear shut-off valves.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open the rear shut-off valves and listen for air escaping.
questions.explanation: Open the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer. If air escapes from these valves, the air brake system is supplying the whole vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do if the spring brakes are on?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.
Press the accelerator.
Turn the steering wheel.
Be careful because the brakes might fail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not press the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. Using both at the same time can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What should you do before inspecting slack adjusters on S-cam brakes?

options.text: Park on a hill and test the brakes.
Put on gloves and push in the slack adjusters.
Remove the drum and look inside.
Place wheel chocks and disengage the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place wheel chocks and disengage the parking brake.
questions.explanation: Park on level ground, place wheel chocks, and disengage the parking brake. Pull each slack adjuster to check it does not move more than about one inch. If it moves more, it needs adjustment.

questions.question: What should you do when checking the engine compartment?

options.text: Do not engage the parking brake.
Place wheel chocks.
Keep the engine running.
Put the gearshift in first gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place wheel chocks.
questions.explanation: Before checking the engine compartment, turn on the parking brakes and place wheel chocks. Check the engine before getting in the cab and starting the engine.

questions.question: How do you release the parking brake?

options.text: Tap the brake pedal three times.
Push in the brake control knob.
Start the vehicle.
Tap the accelerator twice.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push in the brake control knob.
questions.explanation: The parking brake is controlled by a knob. Pull the knob out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about how many feet to stopping distance?

options.text: 32 feet
15 feet
50 feet
10 feet

questions.correctAnswerText: 32 feet
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance includes perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. At 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet.

questions.question: What is one function of the emergency air line?

options.text: Control the emergency brakes.
Flash a light when air pressure is low.
Allow for quick turning.
Control steering in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Control the emergency brakes.
questions.explanation: The emergency air line supplies air to trailer air tanks and controls the emergency brakes on combination vehicles.

questions.question: What should you do when driving through a work zone?

options.text: Slow down.
Speed up.
Use a cell phone.
Steer with one hand.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Follow posted speed limits in work zones. Slow down if road or weather conditions are poor, and slow down more if workers are near the road.

questions.question: What can happen if you use the parking brake in very wet, freezing weather?

options.text: The brakes will squeak.
The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
The brakes may suddenly release.
The brakes may explode.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes may freeze and the vehicle cannot move.
questions.explanation: In very wet weather with freezing temperatures, using the parking brake can cause it to freeze, preventing the vehicle from moving.
